# Motivation and Overview {.unnumbered}


A liquid droplet on a substrate takes on the shape that
minimizes its interfacial energy while its volume stays constant (liquid
is incompressible). Since the liquid/vapor energy is proportional to area, this
leads to a classical *constrained variational problem*:
$$
\min_{\Sigma} \; A[\Sigma] \quad \text{subject to} \quad V[\Sigma] = V_0,
$$ {#eq-problem}
where $\Sigma$ is a surface with a boundary curve (the contact line) on
the substrate, $A[\Sigma]$ is its area, and $V[\Sigma]$ is the enclosed
volume. Wetting adds energies on the contact area with the substrate and
with a rigid obstacle (@sec-interfaces).

Kenneth Brakke's Surface Evolver [@Brakke1992] solves exactly this
problem (and substantially more general variants of it) numerically,
by discretizing the surface as a triangle mesh and iteratively moving
the vertices along the negative gradient of the energy -- a discrete
gradient descent. Our program mirrors the same principle, with two
improvements over the simplest approach: a Sobolev preconditioning of
the gradient (@sec-sobolev) and a penalty formulation of
the volume constraint (@sec-constraint).

**How this document is organized.** *Part I* states the model and derives the mathematics; it
contains no program names or parameter values and would be valid for any
implementation. *Part II* states what the program does with it:
which quantities are computed where, which numerical devices were added
that are *not* implied by the theory, how the output is produced and
how it was checked. Cross-references between the parts point from
each implementation item to the equation it realizes
(@tbl-mapping collects them). *Part III* compares the approach with the
Surface Evolver and lists open directions. *Part IV* explains how to run the
code: installation, the command-line tools, the configuration (with a
reference of every parameter generated from the code), the run-file format
and troubleshooting. The appendix is the project's design log with
measurements behind many of the parameter choices.

The PDF of this document is built by the continuous integration from the
Quarto sources in `docs/`; executable cells generate the parameter
reference and the file-format tables from the code, so they cannot drift.
